text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Opposition parties agreed to hold a vote of no confidence against Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi's government on Monday although they are around 20 seats short of a majority.
- Police interrogated both the former and current central bank presidents on a missing $10 million. Vahur Kraft, current central bank president, refused to answer.
- Vaehi believes opposition politicians plotted against him while on visit to Turkey.
- Estonia will conclude an agreement with Thailand on the extradition and repatriation of drug dealers.
- Former interior minister Heiki Arike will face charges of illegal arms dealing.
- Estonia signed a financial memorandum with EU PHARE programme, under which some 500 million kroons will be granted for various projects.

- Estonia and Sweden collected information about the Estonia ferry disaster, which could improve the work of the emergency services if such a disaster happened again but have failed to implement the proposed changes.
- Britain highly values Estonia's economic reforms, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind told his Estonian counterpart, Toomas Hendrik Ilves, during a visit to London.
- The government does not support the proposed merger of the agriculture, transport and economy ministries.
- Furniture firm Standard is to float some of its stock on the Tallinn Stock exchange.
